title: Tomville — Retro Game View of an AI Agent Team
description: Terminal app (Python + Textual) that shows a team of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) as pixel pets in a retro office; each pet's movement reflects that agent's live status read from herdr (working at its desk, blocked and jumping, idle in the lounge).
Reads the task board from GitHub Issues or a local TASKS.md and animates the handover: the lead assigns a card, workers take it, and it moves through Todo, Doing, Review and Done.
Supports two team shapes, lead + workers and a planner → coder → tester pipeline, each with its own office layout.
tmv CLI builds, starts and stops a team (new, up, down) and handles tasks, messages and health checks (task, send, doctor).

Optional Telegram bot: message the team from a phone, approve agent permission requests with buttons, and get pinged when an agent is blocked or a card is ready for review; no open port, token stored outside the project.
Published on PyPI (pip install tomville, v0.2.1) with 283 tests and CI on Ubuntu and macOS.

title: Desir — LLM-Powered Virtual Assistant
description: Built a real-time, voice-driven assistant on OpenAI Realtime API—streaming speech input with low-latency paths toward tool calls and UI updates.
Designed an orchestrator that routes user intent to specialist sub-agents (email, calendar, web search, messaging, knowledge base) with explicit handoffs instead of one monolithic prompt.
Implemented permission-style gates so sensitive actions (send mail, run OS automation) only fire after user confirmation policies.
Shipped a React/Vite SPA talking to a Python WebSocket backend; orchestration implemented with Pydantic AI for structured outputs and safer tool schemas.
Integrated third-party APIs—Resend for mail, Serper for search—and macOS automation hooks where local actions are required.
Added Logfire traces across orchestrator steps to debug multi-turn failures without guessing which agent dropped context.

title: TTorch — Lightweight Deep Learning Framework (C++/Python)
description: Implemented a tensor library and autograd engine in C++ with Python bindings—PyTorch-style tensors, views, and backward passes, written for clarity.
Built a dynamic computation graph with modular gradient primitives (Add, Multiply, ReLU, Dot) so new ops plug in without rewriting the engine.
Implemented reverse-mode autodiff with correct topological ordering for multi-use tensors.
Packaged as pip install ttorch: Python API → pybind11 bindings → C++ core → autograd.
Automated releases with cibuildwheel and GitHub Actions: 15 wheels for Linux, Windows, and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) on Python 3.11–3.13, published to PyPI on tagged releases.

title: Real-Time Human Emotion Detection Pipeline
description: Two-stage CV pipeline: YOLOv11n finds faces in a webcam stream; a classifier predicts one of seven emotions per face.
Used a frozen ViT-B/16 as a feature extractor (768-D embeddings), feeding a logistic-regression head written from scratch in PyTorch and trained with L-BFGS.
Wrote the training and evaluation loop by hand (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, confusion matrices) and validated across 5 stratified 70/15/15 splits.
Reached 73.5% test accuracy on the Kaggle Facial Expression Dataset, against a 14% chance baseline.

title: Maze-Solving Algorithms Visualizer
description: Interactive React/JavaScript front-end that renders mazes and animates search frontiers as algorithms expand nodes.
Implemented BFS, flood fill, and a randomized search variant with identical interfaces so students can compare behavior apples-to-apples.
Supports configurable grid sizes and procedural wall layouts with deterministic seeds for reproducible demos.
Surfaces stats live—nodes expanded, path length, wall-clock time—to compare asymptotics versus intuition.
Python tooling for batch experiments where needed; UI emphasizes step-by-step pedagogy over black-box runs.
